claims.text: Changing the elemental percentages in HfNbTaTiZr affects its mechanical properties.
The mechanical properties of compositionally varied HfNbTaTiZr can be predicted using a hybrid DOE, in-situ characterization, and DFT/MD approach.
The mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr can be optimized by varying its elemental percentages using the proposed hybrid approach.
Elemental composition and microstructure mediate the mechanical response of HfNbTaTiZr.
Integrating experimental and computational methods can reveal the complex relationships between elemental composition and mechanical properties.
Understanding composition–property relationships enables prediction and optimization of HfNbTaTiZr mechanical properties.
The proposed approach will improve understanding of how changing elemental percentages affects mechanical properties.
The resulting understanding will enable optimization of HfNbTaTiZr for specific applications.
Individual experimental or computational approaches are limited in their ability to resolve complex composition–property relationships.
The exact relationships between elemental composition and mechanical properties in this system are unknown.
The hybrid approach may not fully capture the complexity of the HfNbTaTiZr system.
